body: Rule (from an Opus2 incident on Central, 2026-11-07 00:22:39Z). Never put mailbox or tracker message text inline in a double-quoted shell string. Bash treats backticks and $( ) in the text as command substitution. A message containing `cargo run --release` started a second TermAl build in the main checkout; it was caught before link and the host was unaffected. Pass message bodies through a file written with a single-quoted heredoc (e.g. --message-file), or use the MCP tool, which takes the text as a parameter with no shell involved. The same applies to commit messages and notes passed to CLIs.
